body:
Review pass 18. Epic 5 closed, Epic 6 in flight. crossnobis.R was 7 minutes cold so this is a clean read.

CORRECTNESS IS EXACT. Independent base-R oracle, 3 runs, obs=40, p=5, Toeplitz(0.35), known precision:
  package crossnobis : 0.329503620772
  base-R oracle      : 0.329503620772
  max|diff|          : 5.55e-17
estimand label crossvalidated_squared_mahalanobis_contrast. One doc point: the /features per-channel normalization is a deliberate convention and differs from an unnormalized squared Mahalanobis - worth saying so explicitly where the estimand is documented.

YOUR MONTE CARLO TEST HAS REAL POWER - this is the part I most wanted to check. I replicated test-crossnobis-known.R:275 exactly in base R and ran a correct and a deliberately non-crossvalidated estimator through it:

                     null mean    se        |mean|/se
  correct (CV)       +0.00365     0.00580    0.63
  broken  (not CV)   +0.09791     0.00611   16.03    <- your 4-se gate catches it
  correct, signal arm: |mean - target|/se = 0.25, target 0.237202

A 16-sigma margin against the most likely failure mode. That closes the "zero parameter-recovery tests" finding from my original review, and expect_true(any(estimates[,"null"] < 0)) pins the signed-negative property nicely.

ONE REFINEMENT while the epic is still open. The tolerance is 4 * sd(estimates)/sqrt(replications), computed from the observed data. Your acceptance says "within a PRESPECIFIED Monte Carlo error". An adaptive gate widens with the noise, so a defect that inflates variance without biasing the mean passes - the test currently cannot fail for excess variance.

Measured from your own configuration at replications=120: expected se ~0.0058 (null), ~0.0119 (signal). Pin those as constants, keep the 4-sigma mean gates against them, and add an upper bound on observed se (1.5x expected is a sensible start). Then it fails for bias AND variance inflation, and is prespecified as written.
